Looking at these coordinates, I'm examining a line at latitude 28.16°N running east-west from 86.60°E to 87.15°E. This is in the high Himalayan region near Everest, in Nepal and Tibet.

The line passes through extremely mountainous terrain north of the main Everest peak (which is at 28.0°N, 86.93°E). At 28.16°N, we're on the northern slopes/ridges of the Himalayan massif, crossing high plateaus and passes.

I estimate the elevation profile to show gradually increasing elevation from west to east, peaking in the middle near the Everest meridian, then decreasing again. The terrain appears to be primarily high Himalayan plateau and ridge system at 5,300-6,700m elevation.

- Changtse peak is at ~28.15°N, 86.75°E (7,500m) - very close to this transect
- Makalu is at ~27.89°N, 87.09°E (8,485m)

The elevation profile should show a general rise from the western Tibetan plateau, reaching very high elevations in the central mountain section, and declining toward the east.
